newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN ENERGY DEPT RAPPED FOR SLOW REFORM.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN ENERGY DEPT RAPPED FOR SLOW REFORM.

text.p: The Department of Minerals and Energy was on Wednesday criticised for the lack of progress in finalising the overhaul of policies covering the liquid fuels industry.

Several lobby groups told the parliamentary minerals and energy committee that this was holding up vital investments in the oil industry at a time when demand was growing rapidly and would soon outstrip capacity.
They said the main problem appeared to be a lack of capacity in the department and several groups offered to provide assistance funded by the private sector or donor agencies.

"Sales of petroleum products have been growing at some five percent per annum and there is now a need for significant investment in refining capacity expansion in order to meet the expected demand by the year 2000," South African Petroleum Industry Asociation director Colin McClelland told the committee.

But investment was not likely until there was greater clarity on what the department planned to do about the de-regulation or re-regulation of the industry, rules for the transition period, contractual arrangements to lift synthetic fuels from Mossgas and the long-awaited wholesale margin increase.

The government has been reviewing its policies on the previously over-regulated energy sector since 1994, when the veil of secrecy surrounding the sector was lifted following the lifting of sanctions.
